reviewBoundary: Six original complete ten-gap junior grammar passages, each with seven prompted forms and three one-word gaps. Author reviews tense, clause, spelling and legitimate variants; unknown forms remain reviewable. Same-author check only, not independent teacher/learner calibration.

units.title: An umbrella and two names
units.instruction: Fill each gap with one appropriate word or the correct form of the word in brackets.

materials.title: An umbrella and two names
materials.text:
Last Friday, we ____1____ (find) an umbrella in front of the school hall. It was lying ____2____ front of a bench, with nobody nearby. Two ____3____ (name) had been written on its label, one above the other.

Our teacher asked whether we knew anyone ____4____ name matched either one. I recognised the lower name, but that student had left our class the previous year. I agreed ____5____ (take) the umbrella to the office rather than leave it outside.

The umbrella ____6____ (keep) there until the owner could be found. An office assistant looked ____7____ (careful) at the label. She noticed that the upper name was written in newer ink. It was different ____8____ the name in the old class list I had remembered.

Later, a younger student came to ask about the umbrella. She explained that it had belonged to her brother, who was three years ____9____ (old) than she was, before he passed it to her. The two names were not a mistake; they recorded two owners.

Before returning it, the assistant asked a few questions about its colour and handle. The student's answers matched, so she handed it over. I had learned that old records could help, but I needed to compare ____10____ (they) with what was in front of me.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of find.
questions.explanation: Last Friday requires past found. Find is present and finded is nonstandard.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is in front of. The other prepositions do not complete the printed front of.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of name.
questions.explanation: Two requires plural names. Name is singular and namees is misspelt.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Whose modifies name possessively. The other relative words do not express that possession before name.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of take.
questions.explanation: Agreed takes the to-infinitive to take. The -ing, bare and past forms do not complete agreed.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of keep.
questions.explanation: The singular umbrella receives the keeping action in the past, allowing was kept or had been kept. Kept alone lacks a passive auxiliary and were disagrees with the singular umbrella.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Carefully modifies looked at. Careful is an adjective and carefulness a noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Different from, British different to and comparative different than are all legitimate before this noun phrase. With and of do not express this comparison.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of old.
questions.explanation: Three years older than makes an explicit age comparison. Old is not comparative, oldest superlative, and elder is not used in this predicative than construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of they.
questions.explanation: Compare takes object pronoun them. They is subject form and their possessive.

units.title: A changing sky
units.instruction: Fill each gap with one appropriate word or the correct form of the word in brackets.

materials.title: A changing sky
materials.text:
Our class ____1____ (plan) a short weather record last month. One morning brought such ____2____ unusual mixture of sunshine and showers that we decided to begin immediately. Several ____3____ (window) in our room looked towards the playground, giving us a clear view without going outside.

We used a photograph ____4____ (take) by the teacher as the first entry. It showed wet ground under bright sunlight. Our record would include short descriptions as well ____5____ pictures, because one image could not show how quickly the sky had changed.

Instead of ____6____ (write) only 'good' or 'bad', we described what we could observe. A student ____7____ coat was still damp explained that it had rained heavily on her walk to school, even though the sun was shining now.

We worked more ____8____ (careful) after noticing how easily a general label could hide differences. The final record ____9____ (check) by two classmates before it went on the wall. They corrected one time and moved a photograph beside the matching description.

The project did not make ____10____ (we) weather experts. It helped us distinguish a brief observation from a description of the whole day, and to say when we had actually looked.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of plan.
questions.explanation: Last month locates the action in the past, spelled planned with doubled n. Plan is present and planed is a different verb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Such an unusual mixture takes an before the vowel sound. A has wrong sound agreement and such the is not this construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of window.
questions.explanation: Several requires plural windows. Singular window and misspelt windowes do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of take.
questions.explanation: Taken is a passive participle modifying photograph, with by the teacher. Taking would be active and was taken introduces an unlinked finite clause.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: As well as joins descriptions and pictures. Than, that and and do not complete the printed as well pattern.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of write.
questions.explanation: Instead of takes the -ing form writing. The other forms do not fit after this preposition.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Whose marks possession of the coat. Who, which and that cannot directly modify coat possessively.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: More carefully modifies worked. The adjective and noun forms do not fill the adverb slot.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of check.
questions.explanation: The singular record receives checking in the past, allowing simple or past-perfect passive. Checked alone lacks a passive auxiliary; were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Make takes object pronoun us before weather experts. We is subject and our possessive.

units.title: A programme for the show
units.instruction: Fill each gap with one appropriate word or the correct form of the word in brackets.

materials.title: A programme for the show
materials.text:
Our class ____1____ (receive) an invitation to perform a short play at the junior school. The audience would include younger ____2____ (child), so we wanted a programme that they could understand easily.

We chose a simple design ____3____ showed the characters on one side and the order of scenes on the other. I was responsible ____4____ checking that the names matched the cast list. Another student wrote a short note ____5____ (explain) the story without giving away its ending.

The first version looked attractive, but its letters were very small. We tried a larger type size and removed an unnecessary picture. The second version was more ____6____ (useful) than the first because people could actually read it while waiting for the show.

At the ____7____ (begin) of the performance, I saw a young visitor pointing to a character in the programme. She recognised the same character when the actor came on stage. It was such ____8____ encouraging moment that I forgot how nervous I had been.

Afterwards, we decided ____9____ (thank) the students who had helped with the printing. Our ____10____ (teacher) had also given us advice during rehearsals. We kept one programme with our class photographs, not because it was perfect, but because it showed how many small tasks made the event possible.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of receive.
questions.explanation: The completed invitation starts a past narrative, requiring received. Present receive/receives do not fit that account.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of child.
questions.explanation: A group of younger children needs the irregular plural children. Child lacks a determiner and childs is nonstandard.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: The design is the subject antecedent of a defining relative clause, allowing that or which. Who refers to people, where is not a subject and what does not take this expressed antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Responsible for checking uses for before the -ing phrase. The other prepositions do not complete this expression.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of explain.
questions.explanation: Explaining gives the note's content and to explain its purpose; both fit. Explained would be passive and cannot take the active content object here.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of useful.
questions.explanation: More useful requires the adjective useful after the printed more. Usefully and usefulness are adverb/noun forms.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of begin.
questions.explanation: At the beginning of uses the noun beginning. Begin is a verb and began a finite past form.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Such an encouraging moment uses an before a vowel sound. A has wrong sound agreement and such the is not the construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of thank.
questions.explanation: Decided takes to thank. The other forms do not directly complete decided.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of teacher.
questions.explanation: Our teacher or our teachers can both refer to the advice-giving staff and agree with had given, so both are accepted. Teaches and teaching are not the staff noun in this slot.

units.title: A model of a route
units.instruction: Fill each gap with one appropriate word or the correct form of the word in brackets.

materials.title: A model of a route
materials.text:
By the time our exhibition opened, we ____1____ (spend) two weeks making a model of the route from the school to the sports centre. After ____2____ (try) several layouts, we chose one that left enough space for clear labels.

Our first model had been so crowded ____3____ visitors could hardly follow the path. We had included every tree, bench and street light. The teacher asked whether all those details helped explain the journey.

We checked several ____4____ (measure) again and kept the important turns and crossings. A small symbol marked the place ____5____ people could wait for the group. Visitors were invited to trace the route ____6____ (independent), without a student explaining every step.

When someone hesitated, we encouraged them ____7____ (ask) a question. A parent ____8____ daughter had recently joined the school noticed that one entrance was missing. We added it, then asked another visitor to try the model.

The comments ____9____ (record) during the exhibition and read by the whole class afterwards. We learned that a model could be accurate in many details yet still leave out something a visitor needed. Comparing the two versions helped us understand the ____10____ (different) between showing everything we knew and showing what would help someone else find the way.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of spend.
questions.explanation: By the time of the past opening favours had spent; simple spent also narrates the completed preparation. Spend and singular present-perfect has spent do not fit we in this past account.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of try.
questions.explanation: After as a preposition takes trying, not a bare verb, finite past or to-infinitive.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: So crowded that introduces the resulting difficulty. Than compares rather than gives a result; what and which cannot complete this construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of measure.
questions.explanation: Several requires a plural noun. Measurements and measures can both refer to the recorded dimensions here. Measurement is singular, while measuring and measured do not supply the plural count noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Where introduces the place in which people could wait; locative that is also accepted in a defining place clause. Who refers to people and whose needs a possessed noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of independent.
questions.explanation: Independently modifies trace and is explained by without a student guiding every step. Independent is an adjective and independence a noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of ask.
questions.explanation: Encouraged them takes to ask. The other forms do not complete this pattern.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Whose expresses the parent's relation to daughter. The other words do not supply a possessive determiner.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of record.
questions.explanation: Plural comments receive recording in the past, allowing simple or past-perfect passive. Recorded alone is active and was disagrees with comments.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of different.
questions.explanation: Both difference and differences can name the contrast between the two ways of presenting information. Different/differently are adjective/adverb forms.

units.title: The names in the programme
units.instruction: Fill each gap with one appropriate word or the correct form of the word in brackets.

materials.title: The names in the programme
materials.text:
After ____1____ (choose) a programme design, our drama group sent it for printing. The first copies ____2____ (print) on Thursday, one day before the show. Their large letters were easier to read ____3____ those in the earlier version.

However, one actor's name had been ____4____ (mistake) written with the wrong final letter. The girl ____5____ was playing the narrator noticed it while checking her lines. She did not want a public argument; she simply asked whether we could correct the remaining copies.

We agreed ____6____ (check) the whole cast list rather than change only that one name. Two ____7____ (name) had similar spellings, which explained how the error had happened. ____8____ spite of the limited time, we made a corrected version and checked it with the actors before printing again.

One earlier copy ____9____ (keep) with a note explaining the change. We did not want it to be mistaken for the final programme later. Everyone was ____10____ (busy) than expected that afternoon, but the extra care mattered.

At the show, the narrator thanked us quietly. The correction was small on the page, yet important to the person it named. I learned that checking names was part of respecting the work behind a performance, not merely a final decoration.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of choose.
questions.explanation: After takes choosing in this prepositional phrase. The other forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of print.
questions.explanation: The plural copies receive printing in the past. Printed alone lacks a passive auxiliary; was disagrees with copies.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Easier introduces comparison with the earlier letters, requiring than. As and that do not complete this comparative; then is a time adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of mistake.
questions.explanation: Mistakenly modifies written to describe an error. Mistake is a noun/verb and mistaken an adjective, not the needed adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: The girl is the subject of a defining relative clause, so who or that. Which is inappropriate for the person, where is not a subject and whose lacks a following noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of check.
questions.explanation: Agreed takes to check. The other forms do not directly complete agreed.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of name.
questions.explanation: Two requires plural names. Singular name and misspelt namees do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: The fixed concessive phrase is in spite of. The other prepositions do not complete it.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of keep.
questions.explanation: One copy receives keeping in the past, so singular passive was/had been kept. Kept alone is active, and were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of busy.
questions.explanation: Than requires a comparative. Busier and grammatical more busy are accepted; busy is not comparative, busiest superlative and more busier duplicates comparison.

units.title: A family recipe notebook
units.instruction: Fill each gap with one appropriate word or the correct form of the word in brackets.

materials.title: A family recipe notebook
materials.text:
The oldest page in our family recipe notebook had been ____1____ (write) by my grandmother. Several ____2____ (memory) were attached to it: a birthday meal, a winter visit and a story about a cake that did not rise.

When we decided to make a new copy, I was responsible ____3____ preparing the pages. Before ____4____ (serve) dinner one evening, I asked each person to explain a favourite recipe. My aunt, ____5____ handwriting I could recognise immediately, showed me where she had changed one of Grandma's instructions.

I noticed that two people sometimes described the same dish ____6____ (different). One began with quantities; another began with how the food should look. We decided ____7____ (record) both accounts, clearly naming their owners rather than pretending there was only one family version.

The notebook now contains short stories as well ____8____ recipes. What ____9____ (surprise) me most was how often a small detail brought back a whole occasion. A mark beside one ingredient could lead to a conversation about somebody who had cooked it years earlier.

We kept the original pages and stored ____10____ (they) separately from the new copy. The new book was easier to read, but the old handwriting remained part of the family's record. Making a clear copy did not require removing the signs of how the recipes had travelled between people.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of write.
questions.explanation: Had been takes the past participle written. Wrote is simple past and writing an -ing form.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of memory.
questions.explanation: Several requires plural memories. Memory is singular and memorys is misspelt.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Responsible for preparing uses for. The other prepositions do not complete this expression.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of serve.
questions.explanation: Before as a preposition takes serving, not a bare, past or to-infinitive form.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Whose modifies handwriting possessively in the non-defining clause. Who, which and that do not supply that possession.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of different.
questions.explanation: Differently modifies described. Different is an adjective and difference a noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of record.
questions.explanation: Decided takes to record. The other forms do not directly complete decided.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: As well as links stories and recipes. Than, that and and cannot complete the printed pattern.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of surprise.
questions.explanation: The past narrative normally takes finite surprised in the subject clause. Surprising alone lacks an auxiliary, and base surprise does not agree or mark the past event.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of they.
questions.explanation: Stored takes object them. They is subject form and their possessive.
